checks.comparison: descent_lemma (conditional form): for all x, y, int f(x - gamma g(y,b)) dmu(b) <= f x - gamma/2||grad f x||^2 - gamma/4||grad f y||^2 + gamma L^2/2||x-y||^2 + gamma^2 L/2 sigma^2 (with integrability), i.e. E_{k+1}[f(x^{k+1})] given x = x^k, y = x^{a_k} (accepted fresh-sample reading of L1239). Verified the inequality: smoothness upper bound, unbiasedness, oracle_moments, -<a,b> = -(|a|^2+|b|^2-|a-b|^2)/2, gamma L <= 1/2. expected_descent is the integrated form for the recursion. Constants exactly L1237.

descent_lemma/expected_descent assume 0 <= gamma <= 1/(2L) (source: 0 < gamma <= 1/(2L); allowing gamma = 0 only generalizes) and, for expected_descent, the delayed recursion with a_k <= k and an IID stream.

residual_lemma: (1/(K+1)) sum_{k<=K} E||x^k - x^{a_k}||^2 <= 1/(2L^2(K+1)) sum_{k<=K} E||grad f(x^{a_k})||^2 + gamma/L sigma^2 = L1246. residual_step is L1367's per-k bound 2 delta gamma^2 sum E||grad f(x^{a_j})||^2 + 2 delta gamma^2 sigma^2, window_count the at-most-R counting (L1382). Checked: 2 delta gamma^2 <= 1/(2RL^2) and 2 delta gamma^2 sigma^2 <= gamma sigma^2/L for delta < R.
residual_lemma hypotheses: a_k <= k, k < a_k + R (delays <= R-1), 0 <= gamma <= 1/(2RL), IID, A1, A3.

iteration_bound: for 0 < gamma <= 1/(2RL), a_k <= k < a_k + R: average E||grad f(x^k)||^2 <= 2(f x0 - f^inf)/(gamma(K+1)) + 2 gamma L sigma^2 (L1267). iteration_accuracy: with gamma = stepSize L sigma eps R and K >= 8RL(f x0 - f^inf)/eps + 16 sigma^2 L (f x0 - f^inf)/eps^2: average <= eps (L1272-1280), sigma >= 0, eps > 0, L > 0. Both true.

step_integral: for an IID family xi with law mu and jointly measurable Phi(s,b) depending on s only through s_j, j<k: Phi(xi, xi_k) is P-integrable iff (a.e. integrable in b and the integral of ||Phi|| integrable), and then E Phi(xi, xi_k) = E int Phi(xi, b) dmu(b). This is Fubini for the independent pair (prefix, xi_k) with marginal mu; true and exactly the clause. step_bound is its nonnegative domination corollary.

oracle_moments: ||g y.||^2 integrable and E||g y b||^2 <= sigma^2 + ||grad f y||^2 (variance decomposition with unbiasedness, L1326-1332). iterate_moments: x^k measurable, ||x^k||^2, ||grad f(x^k)||^2, f(x^k) integrable for a_k <= k, under A1 and IsStochasticGradient; diff_sq_integrable for ||x^i - x^j||^2. True (quadratic growth from L-smoothness, induction).

noise_sum: E||sum_{j in [b,m)} (g(x^{a_j}, xi_j) - grad f(x^{a_j}))||^2 <= (m-b) sigma^2 with integrability. Martingale-difference bound (cross terms vanish since x^{a_j} depends on xi_<j and E g = grad f); matches L1366-1367. It omits the differentiability hypothesis, which is not needed (unbiasedness is stated w.r.t. Mathlib's gradient and the Lipschitz bound gives measurability/growth of gradient f).

Prefix dependence: history_congr/delayedIterate_congr (x^k unchanged if xi_j, j<k, unchanged), delayedIterate_measurable (measurable in the stream given jointly measurable g), delayedIterate_telescope (x^m = x^b - gamma sum_{j in [b,m)} g(x^{a_j}, xi_j) for a_j <= j), delayedIterate_succ/zero/history_stable (the recursion). Exactly the clause; all true by induction on the history table.
initial_stationary: ||grad f x0||^2 <= 2L(f x0 - f^inf) under L > 0, differentiability, Lipschitz gradient, lower bound. Exactly L1503.
No extra content.
Justified by L1234.
No extra content.
Justified by L1244/L1371; gamma >= 0 generalizes gamma > 0.
Delta appears as f x0 - lower (identical to SmoothLower.gap at use sites); no extra hypothesis.

Hypotheses (measurability, prefix dependence, nonnegativity/domination in step_bound) are exactly what the statement needs; xi is a general IID family, more general than the coordinate process used in the setups.
Hypotheses: L > 0, differentiability, L-Lipschitz gradient, IsStochasticGradient, IID, a_k <= k; no extra assumption.
No extra assumption.
No extra hypotheses beyond a_k <= k (needed since history returns x^k when a_k > k) and joint measurability of g (from IsStochasticGradient).
No extra content.
Reals L > 0, sigma >= 0, eps > 0, gamma >= 0 (or > 0 where needed); naturals R, K, k; index maps a : N -> N with a_k <= k (and k < a_k + R). R >= 1 is implied by the window hypothesis.
All lemmas are stated for the same delayedIterate g gamma a x0 (fun i => xi i w); iteration_accuracy instantiates gamma := stepSize L sigma eps R; lower plays f^inf and f x0 - lower plays Delta.
Universal statements with hypotheses as explicit binders; conclusions are inequalities (and integrability conjuncts); no conclusion used as hypothesis.
A1 as HasGradientAt + Lipschitz gradient, A2 as lower <= f, A3 as IsStochasticGradient plus IID family; exactly the setups' encodings.
Constants gamma/2, gamma/4, gamma L^2/2, gamma^2 L/2 sigma^2; 1/(2L^2(K+1)), gamma/L sigma^2; 2Delta/(gamma(K+1)) + 2 gamma L sigma^2; 2 delta gamma^2; 2L Delta: all match the source.
Lemmas concern the delayed recursion x^{k+1} = x^k - gamma g(x^{a_k}, xi_k), which Algorithm 5's execution equals (exec unit).
IID family with law mu under P; conditional expectation realized by fresh-sample integration (step_integral); expectations are Bochner integrals with integrability proved alongside.
iteration_accuracy is the averaged bound of Theorem 4.1 for the recursion; packaging into the uniform iterate happens in the public units.
Iterates via the history table; equivalence with the recursion is stated by delayedIterate_succ/zero/history_stable.
Providers (IsStochasticGradient, IID, delayedIterate, history, stepSize) previously inspected; used with their exact meaning.
iteration_bound follows from expected_descent (C1) summed and residual_lemma (C2), as in L1253-1267; iteration_accuracy then follows by the stepsize/horizon algebra.
sigma = 0 handled by stepSize's branch; K = 0 allowed; empty windows (a_k = k) contribute 0; gamma = 0 allowed in C1/C2 (harmless generalization).
